title: Innovation Saturation Does Not Robustify Kalman-Filtered Importance Ratios in LLM Reinforcement Learning

### Reasoning:

#### Purpose:
The contribution tests whether innovation saturation can mitigate Kalman Policy Optimization's (KPO) sensitivity to the process-to-measurement noise ratio \( Q/V \). Paper [1] introduces innovation saturation as a robust filtering technique to address measurement outliers in Kalman filters, but it does not address KPO or sensitivity to \( Q/V \). Paper [3] applies saturation mechanisms iteratively for robust Kalman filtering but does not establish or test the specific relationship between innovation saturation and \( Q/V \) sensitivity in KPO. Paper [5] uses innovation saturation in a variational Bayesian framework for integrated navigation systems but does not test the same relationship. No prior paper explicitly tests the relationship between innovation saturation and \( Q/V \) sensitivity in KPO.

#### Mechanism:
The contribution implements Innovation-Saturated KPO (IS-KPO), which clips the Kalman innovation when it exceeds a scale-aware threshold. Paper [1] proposes an innovation saturation mechanism for robustifying Kalman filters by clipping distorted innovations, which is substantively equivalent to the mechanism described here. Paper [7] applies a similar saturation mechanism to extended Kalman filters (EKF), and paper [3] introduces iteratively saturated Kalman filtering, which also clips innovations for robustness. These mechanisms are substantively equivalent to the clipping approach used in IS-KPO.

#### Evaluation:
The contribution evaluates IS-KPO on MATH-500, measuring its recovery of performance gaps under weak smoothing and statistical significance. This evaluation design uses standard statistical significance testing and performance gap measurement, which are generic experimental moves. Papers [1], [3], and [7] all evaluate innovation saturation mechanisms using similar designs, including performance comparisons and statistical significance testing. While the specific benchmark (MATH-500) is new, the evaluation design itself is covered by prior work.

#### Domain:
The contribution applies innovation saturation to LLM reinforcement learning and policy optimization. Papers [4], [6], [8], [10], and [11] all address reinforcement learning and policy optimization, which is the same general application area. While none of these papers specifically address KPO or LLM reinforcement learning, the domain is covered under the general application area of reinforcement learning and policy optimization.

While [16] and [17] evaluate innovation saturation mechanisms, their setups focus on robustness to outliers and do not involve diagnostic analysis of clipping thresholds or activation rates in KPO. Similarly, [20] and [26] evaluate reinforcement learning methods but do not use this diagnostic design. Thus, the evaluation design is novel.

[12] and [20] both address Kalman filtering in RL contexts, with [12] focusing on policy evaluation and [20] on proximal policy optimization. These papers establish that Kalman filtering has been applied to RL before, even if the specific instance (KPO) differs. Therefore, the domain is covered.
